annotation.title_clean: Virtue Ethics in Robotics: An ethics module to cultivate character and ethical reasoning
annotation.title_en: Virtue Ethics in Robotics: An ethics module to cultivate character and ethical reasoning
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Henslee, E.; Yeaman, A.; Wiinikka-Lydon, J.
annotation.venue: ASEE Annual Conference 2022 (American Society for Engineering Education)
annotation.summary_en: Work-in-progress ASEE conference paper describing a virtue ethics module in a senior Mobile Robotics course at Wake Forest University. It uses rubrics, structured discussions and a role-play case study to build students' ethical reasoning and character virtues (empathy, intellectual humility, practical wisdom) as future AI and robotics professionals.
key_provisions_or_claims: Proposes character education and virtue ethics as an alternative to consequentialist/deontological engineering ethics teaching.
Implements an ethics module in a Mobile Robotics elective using rubrics, 'two questions and a thought' discussions and a role-play case study.
Focuses on 'cumulative' virtues: empathy, intellectual humility, practical wisdom.
Uses pre/post surveys to measure student efficacy in ethical reasoning.
Framework is flexible and transferable to other courses and ethical frameworks.
